For the payment the customer has to enter its payment data and has to wait until the bank confirms the payment.
While waiting for the payment confirmation the customer can enter its shipping address (an independent billing address can be entered if the shipping address is not equal to the billing address).
Finally if the address and the payment steps are executed then the order will be finished by the system.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Build a connected path from each modeled start to an end or intentionally continuing state. Avoid accidental disconnected flow nodes.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

args.text: When the description says a participant waits until an external party confirms or sends a response, model the wait as an intermediate message catch event rather than a task.

result.rule: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.

args.text: When the description says a participant must wait for an external party to confirm or send a response, model that wait as an intermediate catch event rather than as a task.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already states the same modeling rule.

result.rule: When the description says a participant will arrive at an unspecified time and subsequent work depends on that arrival: model the wait for the arrival as an intermediate catch event, not as an event-based gateway waiting for a different outcome

When the description says that a participant sends status updates while an activity is in progress: model each update as an intermediate message catch event in the process flow, rather than as a task, a separate subprocess, or start/end events.

When the description states that a process waits for a later occurrence before the next activity can begin: Model the wait as an intermediate catch event for the described occurrence, placed between the preceding activity and the activity that follows it.

When the description mentions an external person or organization as the recipient of a request, the source of a response or payment, or the destination of a referral, but does not describe that party’s own process or responsibilities: model the stated work and events within the modeled participant; do not create separate participant pools or message flows solely because of that mention
